subject: general
question: 'Natural Levees' are:
solution:
The correct answer is __**depositional landforms of river**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Natural Levees' are depositional landforms of rivers**.
 
• **A natural levee** is formed when silt is pushed to one side by the** movement of a body of water.**
 
• **A river's banks **are frequently just slightly higher than the riverbed.
 
• Sediment, silt, and other debris are pushed aside by the flowing water to build levees along the banks.
 
• **Levees **can help direct the flow of a river because they are often parallel to the river's course.
 
• It can also be constructed or strengthened artificially.
 
• On a flat, cleared surface, piles of dirt, sand, or rocks are typically used to construct artificial levees.
 
• It can also be constructed out of wood, plastic, or metal blocks in areas where rivers flow rapidly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rivers provide erosional landforms **such as river valleys, waterfalls, structural benches, river terraces, river meanders, ox-bow lakes, and peneplains.
 
• **Pediments, Pediplains, Playas, Deflation Hollows, and Caves, as well as Mushroom Rocks, **are examples of **wind-eroded landforms.**
 
• **Erosional Landforms of Wind: Deflation Hollows, Mushroom Rock, Yardang and Zeugen.**
